author: A Robot
objectives: Students will identify and name the four chambers of the heart, the four heart valves, and the major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Students will trace the path of blood through the heart's dual circulation, naming each chamber, valve, and vessel in order.
Students will distinguish the pulmonary circuit from the systemic circuit and explain why the right and left sides of the heart serve different circulatory functions.

Students will explain why the left ventricle has a substantially thicker myocardium than the right ventricle, relating wall thickness to the pressure required to perfuse the systemic versus pulmonary circuits.
Students will describe the function of the atrioventricular and semilunar valves in preventing backflow, and identify which valves separate which chambers or chamber-vessel pairs.

modules.description: An exterior and cutaway view of the human heart, introducing its general orientation and major external features.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Students will identify the anatomical orientation of the heart (right vs. left sides) from a given perspective.
Students will recognize the major vessels connected to the exterior of the heart.
instructions: Observe the two heart models. The left model is an intact exterior view, and the right model is a cutaway view showing internal structures.

clips.changeMeaning: Introduce the intact heart model on the left and the cutaway model on the right.
clips.narration: This is a model of the human heart. The model on the left shows the exterior, while the model on the right is a cutaway view, allowing us to see the internal structures. Notice how the heart is oriented in the chest, with the apex pointing down and slightly to the left, from the patient's perspective.
